Messages.Author: Tomas
Messages.Body:
Can you use Creepshow casino twice on the same action if you untap it with house of Sorrows?

Creepshow Casino
Type: Master
Pool Cost: 2

Master: unique location.
Tap when a vampire you control announces an undirected action to give that acting vampire +1 stealth; usable even though the stealth is not yet needed.

House of Sorrow
Type: Master
Pool Cost: 1

Master: unique location.
Tap to untap any card you control that is not a minion. If you do so, neither that card nor this location untap as normal on your next untap phase.

Messages.Author: Chaitan
Messages.Body:
Yes. Cards and effects stack by default unless rules or card text state otherwise.

But you must tap it twice during the "announces an undirected action" window.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> Tomas wrote:
> Can you use Creepshow casino twice on the same action if you untap it with house of Sorrows?
>
No.
Preceding examples:  [LSJ 20081229] and  [LSJ 20090731] refer to the word "when" for the reason not to be able to use a card twice on a triggered event (Tower of London was the first question like this).

Messages.Author: KevinM
Messages.Body:
I think the issue is that ANY word describing timing means that the effect can only be used once.

c.f. Maris Streck: "...can burn a blood to give a blocking minion +1 intercept."

c.f. Corpse Minion: "...may burn X blood to get +X intercept..."

Neither have such a word.

Messages.Author: direwolf
Messages.Body:
Would it also be a valid argument that the "as announced" window does not allow you to tap the Barrens or Fragment of the Book of Nod (or any other similar effect.)

Also, you do not refresh your hand during this window (IE drawing a Seduction from the action card, or you must have a weapon in hand to play Concealed Weapon.)

That mostly comes into play when someone plays a master card and another player taps the Barrens to dig for a Sudden Reversal. However, it should work both ways: you can't tap the House of Sorrows to untap the Creepshow Casino in the "as announced" window.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> direwolf wrote:
> Would it also be a valid argument that the "as announced" window does not allow you to tap the Barrens or Fragment of the Book of Nod (or any other similar effect.)
>
> Also, you do not refresh your hand during this window (IE drawing a Seduction from the action card, or you must have a weapon in hand to play Concealed Weapon.)
>
> That mostly comes into play when someone plays a master card and another player taps the Barrens to dig for a Sudden Reversal. However, it should work both ways: you can't tap the House of Sorrows to untap the Creepshow Casino in the "as announced" window.
>
Wrong.

Cards aren't replaced in the "as played" window (Rulebook 1.6.1), but you replace your Govern before deciding whether or not to play your Seduction. You can tap Barrens before playing Seduction.

Concealed Weapon is also replaced before putting the weapon in play, but *you need the weapon in your hand in order to play CW in the first place*.

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
So, let's suppose..

I play Jack of both side for a Magnum .44

I get blocked by a vampire with 6 raptor. I discard my hand, including the magnum, play torrent, continue my action, draw another Magnum. Can I equip it ?

(if not, this is a nightmare to ascertain "cheating" by people ; and if there were a way to make discard at random during the time between announce and resolution, it will be even more fun, since the active player will have to keep mental track of which magnum he have in hand is the good one, to know whether he discarded the one for the action or any other)

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
Yes.
The thing is that you fully announce your action: "I play Jack of Both Sides to equip with a .44 Magnum from my hand." (not "this .44 Magnum") In order to be legal, you must have a .44 Magnum in hand when you announce it.
Then, upon resolution, you move a .44 Magnum from your hand to the vampire (if you can).

The thing is that it's not necessarily the same Magnum because you don't have to explicitely say which Magnum you equip (it's irrelevant). As long as you play the named card, it's ok.
